ranked.headline: Genomic knowledgebases add programmatic access, AI curation and containerised deployment
ranked.summary: NAR database-issue updates (CIViC, DGIdb, FusionGDB, VEuPathDB, CNCB-NGDC) appear alongside new APIs and storage formats for cohort-scale genomic data.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is maturation of community genomic resources toward machine-accessible, reproducible infrastructure. Several knowledgebase updates emphasise interoperability: DGIdb adds Python/R clients, Docker images and versioned releases; CIViC introduces Feature entities, Molecular Profiles, AI-guided curation and ClinVar submission; VEuPathDB reports 2,602 datasets, AI-assisted curation and a PostgreSQL migration. FusionGDB 3.0 integrates RNA-seq and WGS breakpoints for 156K fusion genes and generates personalised fusion protein sequences. CNCB-NGDC adds thirteen resources, and CiliaHub curates over 2,500 ciliary genes with ClinVar and orthology data. Programmatic access extends to project data: pyGENIE wraps AACR GENIE files with TMB and signature analysis, and the IGVF Data Portal exposes knowledge-graph-integrated results via an API including agentic-tool support. On the storage side, pbzarr proposes Zarr for per-base data across thousands of samples, reported smaller and faster than D4 and bigWig. Met4All packages Infinium methylation analysis as a dockerised Shiny app.

ranked.headline: Biomedical predictors move toward cross-cohort testing and standardized benchmarks
ranked.summary: PRTS and TabBioMed test prediction across cohorts and curated datasets, while TISCH3, DriverDBv5 and PDAC BioPortal expand reference data.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is that evaluation design limits what a biomedical predictive claim can support. PRTS, a 220M-parameter in-context learning model, predicts clinical endpoints from bulk transcriptomes across diseases and platforms without per-cohort training. TabBioMed standardizes preprocessing across 94 curated public tabular datasets and compares 23 models. Foundation models lead, but tree-based methods remain relevant baselines. Elflow pairs automated QC with VICReg self-supervised representations and is benchmarked on public flow and CyTOF datasets. HIT-Fuse addresses missing modalities when fusing six omics and pathomics inputs. SpaceMACE adds spatial context to tumour-cell annotation. A parallel strand expands the reference data these evaluations depend on. TISCH3 grows to 477 tumour-microenvironment datasets, including 69 spatial collections. DriverDBv5 examines whether multi-omics drivers carry prognostic weight. PDAC BioPortal integrates bulk, single-nucleus and spatial pancreatic cancer cohorts. What is new is the emphasis on cross-platform transfer and standardized comparison. These items do not establish whether curated public benchmarks reflect performance under deployment conditions.

ranked.headline: New reference genomes and clade databases for seep tubeworms, seaweeds, planarians, corals
ranked.summary: Two de novo assemblies (tubeworm, red seaweed) appear alongside NAR database releases for planarians and stony corals, expanding non-model genomic infrastructure.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is genomic infrastructure for non-model eukaryotes, mostly marine. Two preprints report primary de novo assemblies. The first is a draft genome of the seep tubeworm Lamellibrachia satsuma, assembled and annotated from Oxford Nanopore and Illumina data. At 665 Mb in 6,320 scaffolds, it is draft rather than chromosome-level. The second is a reference genome for the red seaweed Furcellaria lumbricalis, which ranges from saline NE Atlantic waters into the brackish Baltic. That distribution makes the genome relevant to salinity adaptation. Two NAR database papers work at the clade level. PlanMine 4.0 adds new planarian genomes, 70 flatworm transcriptomes and expanded expression resources. CoralDB integrates functional and evolutionary multi-omics data for stony corals, which are reef foundation species with little integrative multi-omics characterization. Together, these releases pair single-species references with curated, queryable platforms. That supports comparative and evolutionary genomics in taxa that lack mature model-organism resources.

ranked.headline: Workflow and reference tooling for microbial species typing, profiling and genome comparison
ranked.summary: New workflows target species assignment, nanopore 16S interoperability, SNP transmission clustering and MGnify v6 amplicon, viral and mobilome analyses.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is packaging microbial identification and comparison methods into reproducible, accessible tooling. For species designation, Robust Cluster Typing uses ribosomal proteins in a Snakemake/Python workflow to assign genomes to species-level clusters, shown on Campylobacter. RADSuite pairs RADlib, a curated 16S rRNA gene copy database, with RADx, which identifies sequenced variable regions for species-level identification. VPHYL converts Emu and EPI2ME wf-16s nanopore abundance tables into phyloseq or BIOM objects with HTML reports. SNP2Cluster-Py offers pathogen-agnostic, context-aware core SNP and transmission-cluster analysis, tested on Klebsiella and pneumococcal WGS. At resource scale, MGnify v6 adds amplicon variant analysis, expanded viral and mobilome annotation, Nextflow/Prefect automation and improved programmatic access. Deployment and genome comparison are addressed by Sparrowhawk, a WebAssembly framework for local, private browser tools, and nf-core/pairgenomealign, a Nextflow wrapper for LAST pairwise whole-genome alignment. Scopes differ; no cross-tool performance comparisons are reported.

ranked.headline: Association and prediction methods jointly model variant classes, phenotypes and scales
ranked.summary: New methods fuse predicted expression with rare-variant kernels, learn phenotype scales, ensemble PRS, and test interactions across multiple binary traits.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is genetic association and prediction that combines information sources rather than relying on marginal single-variant tests or fixed modeling choices. PrediXSKAT embeds PrediXcan-predicted expression into the SKAT kernel, jointly testing rare coding and common cis-regulatory variants to improve gene-level power. GiMat extends multivariate kernel regression to test SNP gene-gene interactions across multiple dichotomous phenotypes. SIQReg learns a phenotype scale transformation minimizing quantile heterogeneity, improving GWAS, TWAS and polygenic prediction in UK Biobank. On the prediction side, a regularized ensemble framework builds polygenic risk scores from GWAS summary statistics alone and outperforms existing PRS methods. A related preprint fine-tunes Borzoi and AlphaGenome on admixed-population genomes and RNA-seq, finding they match, rather than exceed, variant-based linear models for expression prediction, which bears on the expression-imputation step that TWAS-style approaches such as PrediXSKAT depend on. Three works are published; PrediXSKAT and the sequence-model comparison are preprints.

ranked.headline: Causal discovery methods benchmarked under latent confounding and perturbation data
ranked.summary: New benchmarks test temporal and interventional causal discovery on simulated kinetic and CRISPR perturbation data, exposing partial-observability limits.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is systematic benchmarking of causal discovery for biological networks rather than new algorithm development. One preprint evaluates tMIIC, PCMCI+/LPCMCI and SVAR-FCI on simulated biochemical kinetic models, contrasting fully observed settings with partially observed ones containing latent confounders and unobserved variables. A published study compares interventional causal structure learning algorithms on synthetic and CRISPR perturbation data for gene regulatory network inference. Together they probe how temporal and interventional information affect recovery of causal structure. Three other preprints (BI-SCUDO Regression, DeepCINET, siGMA) address noise-aware or rank-based prediction from omics and screening data; they relate through noise handling but do not benchmark causal network inference.

ranked.headline: Ground-truth simulation, annotation scoring and pangenomes anchor comparative genomics evaluation
ranked.summary: New tools supply ground-truth simulation and annotation quality scoring, while a C. elegans pangenome shows what gene-content variation benchmarks must capture.
ranked.synthesis: The items address different problems, but the dominant thread is infrastructure for evaluating and interpreting gene-level comparative data. OrthoSimulator generates empirically calibrated datasets with known orthogroups and gene trees, giving ground truth for orthology inference benchmarks. ABAQS scores genome annotation quality through completeness, gene model validity and protein profile accuracy, and is applied to more than 1700 fungal genomes. On the biological side, the 140-strain C. elegans pangenome reveals extensive gene copy-number variation in hyper-divergent regions, and WormIE integrates multi-source C. elegans annotations for gene-list and RNA-seq interpretation. What is new is pairing explicit truth or quality metrics with resources that expose gene-content variation, so annotation and orthology methods can be validated against realistic complexity.

ranked.headline: Standard metrics and same-platform validation overstate clinical model performance
ranked.summary: New analyses show AUC misses diagnosis timing and same-modality validation inflates miRNA classifiers, while a calibrated epigenetic clock targets a regional population.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is that conventional evaluation can misrepresent clinical model utility. The mammography preprint reports that AUC and C-index for breast cancer risk models are insensitive to diagnosis timing, and proposes a two-stage whether-versus-when model. The glioblastoma circulating miRNA preprint tests CTGAN and TVAE augmentation and finds that same-modality validation overstates performance, with cross-platform AUROC around 0.40-0.47, near chance. The published epigenetic clock study addresses a related issue of population specificity: a SuperLearner trained on non-Nicoyan Costa Ricans is used to calibrate age acceleration for the Nicoya blue zone. Together the items point to timing, cross-platform transfer and population calibration as properties that discrimination metrics alone do not capture. Two of the three items are preprints, so those findings remain provisional.

ranked.headline: Analysis and representation choices shape apparent findings in neuroimaging and brain-model evaluation
ranked.summary: Three preprints show that parameterization, null models and prompt cues can drive apparent neuroimaging results, motivating stricter validation of analysis pipelines.
ranked.synthesis: The shared thread is that upstream representation and analysis decisions determine what neuroimaging results appear to show. The rich-club EEG study finds that null network construction and hub re-identification can create or erase apparent Alzheimer's group differences. The LLM connectivity-graph probe reports that ADHD predictions from rs-fMRI graphs follow class bias and prompt cues rather than subject-specific connectivity. The corpus callosum framework addresses representation directly, resampling the midsagittal callosum onto a standardized grid for diffusion MRI to avoid inter-subject misalignment. What is new is the emphasis on testing whether outputs depend on analysis choices or surface cues rather than on biological structure. All three are preprints, so the findings remain preliminary and unreplicated.

ranked.headline: Sequence-only affinity prediction coexists with GPU-accelerated and consensus-based structural tools
ranked.summary: Savant predicts affinity from sequence and SMILES alone, while GPU scoring, flow matching and consensus selection refine structure-based modeling.
ranked.synthesis: Savant is the clearest structure-free item: it predicts protein-ligand dissociation constants from amino acid sequence and SMILES without structure, docking or GPU, and uses a leakage-controlled evaluation. The other items are structure-oriented and show a looser common thread of computational efficiency and pose quality. ShEPhERD-score provides GPU-accelerated differentiable 3D similarity scoring and alignment, benchmarked on DUDE-Z. CrypticFlow uses hierarchical flow matching with Cartesian C-alpha anchors and internal-coordinate midpoints for apo-to-holo generation. AbPoolRank selects antibody-antigen models from mixed predictor pools by cross-pose agreement and geometry. Infernal-GPU parallelizes covariance-model search for RNA, and TopoPPI maps interfaces into low-distortion 2D atlases. The summaries give no quantitative comparisons, so relative performance of structure-free and structure-based routes remains unestablished.

ranked.headline: Explicit network, ODE, Bayesian and causal models are used to infer regulatory structure from expression data
ranked.summary: New preprints and papers pair explicit model structure with expression data to infer feedback, transcription kinetics, copy number and spatial causality.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of explicit model structure to extract regulatory or causal organization from expression measurements. Three preprints illustrate this: a systematic analysis of gene network topologies identifies feedback loops as drivers of restored heterogeneity from homogeneous populations; a semi-mechanistic ODE transcription model of zebrafish maternal-to-zygotic transition is fitted to RNA-seq to define expression clusters; and causal-discovery algorithms applied to Visium liver data model local and neighbor-derived effects in senescence. Echidna adds a Bayesian hierarchical model integrating scRNA-seq with bulk WGS to infer copy number alterations across samples and treatment time points. A 161-method cell-cell communication review, the LACA and CellStressDB resources, and a Shapley-explained chromatin imaging study are related context rather than mechanistic expression models.

ranked.headline: Software links GWAS, eQTL and single-cell data to prioritize cell types and effector genes
ranked.summary: Nine tools and resources integrate human genetics with single-cell, spatial and bulk omics for gene and cell-context prioritization.
ranked.synthesis: The items do not form an isoform-resolved thread; the dominant theme is software that connects human genetic or perturbation signals to cell and tissue context. EPIC2 ranks trait-relevant cell types by combining GWAS summary statistics with single-cell chromatin accessibility under LD. CAS-X and CELL-X prioritize type 2 diabetes effector genes using multi-tissue eQTL fine-mapping and islet single-cell atlas data, respectively. CellColocDB and the IGVF Catalog provide queryable resources, the latter a knowledge graph of ~3B nodes and 8.6B edges with an LLM interface. Methodological tools include RapidGLM (2.5-17.8x faster count regression), spicyR v2 (permutation-free co-localisation), ARC-Impute (spatial gene imputation) and CATEomics (CATE model selection). None of the items addresses isoform resolution.

ranked.headline: EEG decoding is tested for transfer across subjects, stimuli and deployment, with controls exposing spurious accuracy
ranked.summary: New preprints stress cross-subject transfer, adaptation cost and sham controls, showing decoding accuracy may not hold beyond the conditions where it was measured.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is whether EEG and neural decoding performance holds outside the conditions in which it was measured. ReBrain transfers an intracranial EEG prior to scalp signals without paired data or fine-tuning, and AMRT reports cross-subject generalization for continuous motor decoding. The BCI study frames adapting frozen EEG encoders as a resource-priced decision using gated Bayesian heads. The EEG-video study is most explicit on validity: contrastive alignment beats CCA for seen stimuli but not novel videos, and a sham control shows accuracy can be spurious. NeuroSim adds a simulator with injected disease biomarkers for classifier development. What is new is the emphasis on transfer, adaptation cost and negative controls. None of the items tests a causal or mechanistic account, so mechanistic validity remains open.

ranked.headline: Nucleic acid foundation models are tailored to taxa, RNA classes and controllable design tasks
ranked.summary: New preprints and papers pair pretrained nucleotide models with domain corpora, mechanistic priors and steering for regulatory DNA, ncRNA, lncRNA and codon design.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is specialization of nucleotide foundation models beyond generic embeddings. GPN is pretrained on 455 apicomplexan assemblies to improve epigenomic prediction in P. falciparum. B-RANKO (150M parameters, bidirectional decoder-only) targets ncRNA generation and representation, and LncRFM contributes LncCorpus and LncBench for lncRNA prediction, reporting gains over RNA foundation models. MARRI adds opening penalties and hybridization gains to cross-RNA attention for RNA-RNA interactions. A second strand concerns controllable generation: GENECraft couples a genomic language model with a functional oracle without training, ARCADE steers activations to control CAI, minimum free energy and GC content, and GenNA conditions generation on natural-language annotations across 2221 eukaryotic species. The items differ in task and architecture, but converge on domain-matched data and explicit control.

ranked.headline: Population-specific variant catalogs and graph tooling make curated genomic references more queryable
ranked.summary: New resources cover underrepresented Indian variation, public 1000 Genomes haploblock hashes, and fast genome graph retrieval, extending queryable reference data.
ranked.synthesis: The items share a focus on making curated genomic reference data more accessible and queryable. GI-DB provides a variant database for the ethnolinguistically and biogeographically diverse Indian population, which is underrepresented in global genomic resources. The Genomic Cluster Engine dataset releases haploblock-based genomic hashes and clusters for 2,548 1000 Genomes individuals as a public resource. gfaidx addresses access at the infrastructure level, indexing GFA genome graphs for low-memory retrieval of gene-sized subgraphs and haplotypes, and is reported as over 100-fold faster than ODGI and vg. What is new is the pairing of population-specific coverage and shared derived datasets with tooling for efficient retrieval. The provided summaries give no further quantitative evaluation of the resources beyond the gfaidx speed claim, which is a preprint report.

ranked.headline: Probing internals of structure predictors while extending generative and inverse folding models
ranked.summary: New work dissects AlphaFold 3 and OpenFold internals and PLM representations while extending protein generation and design with structure-derived priors.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is mechanistic scrutiny of deep learning models for protein structure and sequence. AlphaInterp reports that a few divergent MSA homologues suffice to recover AlphaFold 3 structure, tied to pairformer latent geometry. A separate preprint probes OpenFold's 48 Evoformer layers with four decoders, tracking distance decodability, TM-score reconstruction, and triangle-inequality violations. A third preprint benchmarks ESMC interpretability against curated residue-level annotations, finding that conclusions depend on depth, probe, neuron and SAE choices. Alongside, generative and design models use structure- or sequence-derived priors: FoldMapper (structure-derived evolutionary profiles, multiscale graph encoder), MANTA (language-model geometric priors for IDP ensembles), and A2Holo (dual-stream flow matching for apo-to-holo transitions). New here is quantitative layer-wise probing rather than a shared algorithm.

ranked.headline: Interpretable ADMET models and simulated binding data target peptides and macrocycles
ranked.summary: Preprints on cyclic peptide ADMET, simulated peptide binding data and PTM-aware drug response appear alongside updated ADMET databases for ADCs and drugs.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is machine learning for peptide and macrocycle pharmacology, with interpretability and data supply as the main concerns. AIO targets ADMET prediction for cyclic peptides and macrocycles with an interpretable multimodal framework using solvent-aware contrastive pretraining. VReceptor simulates sequence-dependent peptide binding data via pharmacophore-inspired weighting, as a source of training data. PTM-BDL is adjacent rather than peptide-specific: it combines typed PTM states with sequence, structure and drug features to predict drug response, with site-level integrated-gradients attributions. ADCdb 2.0 (542 antibody-drug conjugates) and DrugMAP 3.0 are reference databases that add ADMET endpoints alongside clinical or bioactivity data. The summaries do not show these resources being combined with the models.

ranked.headline: Computational analysis of RNA sequence and structure across genomes, pathogens and expression systems
ranked.summary: Comparative motif screens and an S. aureus sRNA atlas sit beside studies of RNA folding in host mRNA partitioning and 5' UTR-mediated translation.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is computational analysis of RNA sequence and structure, applied to genomes, transcriptomes and design problems. Two preprints apply comparative and integrative methods. A CMfinder and R-scape screen identifies seven candidate structured ncRNA motifs across protist genomes. aureoRNA integrates phylogeny, public transcriptomes and computational predictions into an interactive atlas of S. aureus sRNAs and their targets. The published items are less directly about ncRNA discovery. A Cell study reports that RNA folding drives species-dependent host mRNA partitioning in Ebola virus condensates. A Bioinformatics study models how promoter choice alters 5' UTR-mediated translation in E. coli and introduces the web service UTR Designer Pro. Preprint findings remain provisional.

ranked.headline: Curated biomedical knowledgebases add ML prioritization and graph integration to expanded coverage
ranked.summary: Four November 2026 resources pair larger curated data with predictors, negative sets or graph reasoning for drug discovery, PPI and plant resistance gene analysis.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is established curated resources expanding coverage while adding layers for computational reuse. canSAR 2026 integrates ML predictors, druggability tools and agentic-AI protein tools. HIPPIE 3.0 reaches about 1.2M experimentally supported human PPIs and adds negative training sets, which supports interaction-prediction training. PRGdb 5.0 grows to 874,967 candidate plant resistance proteins and adds DREM deep-learning prioritization. The IDKG preprint takes a different route: it unifies 20 infectious-disease drug discovery sources in a queryable Neo4j graph (4.6M nodes, 26M edges) for graph-based reasoning. The items differ in domain and architecture; the shared pattern is pairing curation or integration with machine-facing, predictive functionality, not a uniform AI component.

ranked.headline: Brain cell-type molecular atlases are paired with tools linking them to disease, development and connectivity
ranked.summary: Curated atlases and web tools now tie brain cell-type expression to disease, development, spatial and connectome context across mouse and human datasets.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is infrastructure that makes cell-type-resolved brain molecular data reusable and interpretable in context. Resource work includes harmonized sample metadata for wild-type and Alzheimer's disease model mouse sc/snRNA-seq, a multi-omic QTL atlas from 231 human prefrontal cortex donors connecting disorder risk to cell-type and developmental regulation, and scCVD, which spans 701 samples and over 4.68 million cells with scRNA-seq and ATAC-seq for cerebrovascular disease. Tools extend interpretation to other layers: SCOUBI uses a neural network to map axon-dendrite interfaces from extrasomatic RNA in mouse spatial transcriptomics, VEGABrain projects bulk RNA-seq onto developing human brain atlas surfaces with precomputed ssGSEA maps, and CSDX links human expression to mouse connectome strength. Species, tissue and modality vary across these works.

ranked.headline: Expanded databases map RNA 3D structures, viral protein folds and protein domain families
ranked.summary: Recent releases expand structure and annotation resources for RNA, viral proteins, endogenous retroviruses and conserved protein domains.
ranked.synthesis: The four items are curated reference resources that consolidate structural or annotation data into maintained collections. RR3DD 2.0 classifies 15,764 RNA 3D structure chains into 1,042 clusters by RMscore and maps them to Rfam. BFVD v3 provides ColabFold-AlphaFold2 predicted structures for viral proteins as a structural atlas. ERV Navigator integrates human endogenous retrovirus annotations, nomenclatures and genomic loci within a phylogenetically informed framework. The NCBI Conserved Domain Database 2026 update describes revised domain and family models, curation, precomputed annotations and search services. The shared element is infrastructure for structural and evolutionary annotation rather than a single method. Each resource targets a different molecular class, and the new content lies in expanded coverage and integration with existing classifications such as Rfam and established endogenous retrovirus nomenclature.

ranked.headline: Graph and k-mer representations replace linear references in genome inference
ranked.summary: Recent preprints apply graph and k-mer representations to haplotype assignment, ancestry, and relatedness without relying on variant calls.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the replacement of linear-reference coordinates and variant-call inputs with graph or k-mer representations. GRASER phases graph-aligned short reads directly against individual haplotype paths, using unique graph edges to avoid linear-reference bias. KORUS infers ancestry from k-mer Bloom filter representations without variant calls, supporting classification, admixture fractions, and population structure. The fastpmr method computes pairwise mismatch rates for relatedness inference, reported as more than 1000-fold faster than READv2 and applied to screening the global ancient DNA record. What is new is the direct use of graph paths and k-mer sets for haplotype and population-level inference. MitoArc and GapCNV address adjacent problems, namely a reproducible Nextflow workflow for human mtDNA with NUMT-aware evaluation and CNV detection in low-input sequencing data, respectively.

ranked.headline: Cell-type-resolved assays couple epigenetic and transcriptional states to identity
ranked.summary: New single-cell and bulk long-read methods now measure histone marks, methylation and Cas9 edits alongside cell identity.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is resolving regulatory state by cell type. TrES-seq jointly profiles scRNA-seq with nanobody-Tn5 readouts of histone marks (H3K27ac, H3K27me3, H3K9me3), COMET assigns individual bulk long reads to cell types using cell-type-specific methylation, and Superb-seq captures Cas9 edits alongside single-cell transcriptomes in K562 cells. A pan-cancer single-cell lncRNA atlas of over 370,000 cells across 18 cancer types links lncRNAs to regulons, CRISPR screens and survival. Siphon-seq and the full-length heart isoform atlas extend the methodological range to purity-aware platelet RNA-seq and isoform-level diversity, and the remaining items in this set address different questions. What is new is the coupling of perturbation, epigenomic or isoform readouts to cell identity.

ranked.headline: Generative and enhanced-sampling methods model biomolecular conformational ensembles
ranked.summary: BioEmu2 emulates biomolecular dynamics far faster than MD, while enhanced-sampling studies resolve multimodal binding landscapes in disordered regions.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is the shift from single static structures toward conformational ensembles and dynamics. BioEmu2 generates atomically resolved structures and dynamics at sampling rates far above molecular dynamics. The FCP1 study applies OneOPES enhanced-sampling MD to a disordered region binding Rap74, revealing a multimodal conformational landscape and introducing a Divide et impera free-energy decomposition. ProtFlap approaches flexibility from the static side, predicting residue-level flexibility from single structures with an atomic energy-based graph neural network trained on RMSF labels. The AlphaFold analysis of experimentally validated non-globular proteins shows where static predictions diverge from biologically relevant states, which bears on the limits of single-structure models. GlycoMarinate extends the toolkit to coarse-grained Martini 3 modelling of N-glycoproteins. What is new is the use of generative emulation and explicit free-energy decomposition of multimodal binding, although the items do not establish a shared benchmark across these methods.

ranked.headline: Evaluating long-read assembly and variant calling strategies across data types
ranked.summary: Newly posted preprints benchmark long-read SV calling on HiFi and ONT data while new tools target raw nanopore signals and RNA isoform structure.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the evaluation of long-read analysis under data-type-dependent conditions. A preprint benchmarks five local-assembly consensus strategies for long-read human structural variant calling on simulated and real HiFi and ONT data, and reports performance that depends on the data type. Methodological work extends the long-read toolkit in a distinct direction: HARICOT assembles raw nanopore signals without basecalling, using fuzzy de Bruijn graphs and Hough-transform overlap detection, and genomic tessellations introduce a tessellated BWT index intended for faster long-read mapping. Adjacent items address short-read RNA data, where TERRACE 2.0 assembles circular RNAs by combining back-splice and outward-facing paired-end reads, and a published Drosophila study with improved TEChim analysis reports intronic transposons forming alternative exons in brain isoforms, rebutting Azad et al. These items are heterogeneous, so the shared element is calibration and methodological scrutiny rather than a single unified benchmark.

ranked.headline: Haplotype-resolved references reshape association and expression analysis
ranked.summary: Recent pig, Capsicum, apple and pedigree studies show haplotype-aware references changing downstream genetic and expression inference.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is the replacement of a single linear reference with haplotype-resolved assemblies and pangenome graphs, and the propagation of that representation into downstream inference. In the apple study, a matched parent-of-origin-resolved Granny Smith genome changes RNA-seq differential expression and the biological conclusions drawn from it. The Capsicum workflow uses a graph pangenome to localize k-mer GWAS hits and link capsaicinoid and aroma traits to haplotypes and candidate loci. PolyOrigin2 addresses the upstream haplotype reconstruction step in multi-generational diploid and tetraploid pedigrees. The pig pan-genome, with three T2T and sixteen high-quality assemblies, extends this to centromere evolution, structural variation and genotype-phenotype mapping. The new element is the integration of haplotype-aware representation across reference construction, association testing and expression analysis, although the items occupy different stages of this pipeline.

ranked.headline: Host context and diet shape mobile elements and genome content in gut bacteria
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications map plasmid, phage and metabolic determinants of gut bacterial genome content across large cohorts.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how mobile genetic elements and host or environmental context structure gut bacterial genomes. The ETEC preprint reports contrasting plasmid-host associations that shape the distribution of enterotoxigenic E. coli colonization factors. The TwinsUK study assembles a 116,740-vOTU phage catalogue from 1,069 gut metagenomes and links phage genomic variation to bacterial species and microbial metabolites. Genome-scale models of 105 C. difficile strains show that diet shifts commensal interactions more than strain differences do, although this work addresses metabolic interplay rather than mobile elements directly. Other studies extend the scope: MiSA detects disease-associated spatial dysbiosis in HiPR-FISH images, and metaEukaryome uses mitochondrial and plastid sequences to detect eukaryotes across 75,727 global metagenomes. Together these point to host and environmental context as key determinants of gut genome content, though only the ETEC and phage studies examine mobile elements explicitly.

ranked.headline: Core sequence, literature and omics databases report 2026–2027 infrastructure updates
ranked.summary: Public sequence, literature, and metabolomics resources report expanded scale and automated annotation or validation in 2026–2027 updates.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the upkeep of large public biological data resources, where content growth is paired with updates to submission, transfer, validation, and annotation infrastructure. The tRNAdb 2026 release extends a compilation of tRNA sequences and genes that originated as an extension of Sprinzl's seminal collection. Europe PMC's 2026 update reports 48M open abstracts with text-mined and new machine-learning annotations plus expanded identifier handling. MetaboLights describes 2027 developments including a submission workflow, Globus transfers, a validation framework, and dataset reuse support. INSDC reports that its global nucleotide archive now exceeds 75 PB, alongside new governance, a membership pathway, and planned AI-assisted metadata work. What is new is the explicit engineering of automated ingestion, validation, and machine-assisted annotation within resources of this scale. The items are heterogeneous, and the dominant thread applies most directly to the MetaboLights and Europe PMC entries.

ranked.headline: Perturbation response models are tested for transfer and calibrated evaluation
ranked.summary: Recent CRISPRi perturbation studies test whether predictive models transfer across cell lines and hold up under calibrated evaluation metrics.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is how predictive models of perturbation response are evaluated and how far their outputs carry beyond the fitting setting. The Virtual Cell Challenge 2026 metrics are calibrated on experimental repeats for zero-shot CRISPRi transcriptional response prediction, anchoring evaluation to measured reproducibility. The CASTER study addresses transfer of CRISPRi knockdown responses across four human cell lines and reports that adaptation requires screening part of each target line, making transfer conditional rather than automatic. OCCAM and GAIN focus on model architecture: OCCAM combines denoised single-cell representations with gene interaction, text and protein features, while GAIN decomposes combinatorial responses into an additive baseline plus a learned interaction term. CIRCE uses Boltzmann distributions over Hamming distance to infer graded signaling activity. Taken together, the shared element is an explicit reliability question: calibrated metrics and transfer conditions are reported alongside predictive performance.

ranked.headline: Reference-free scoring of protein-protein interface similarity in molecular dynamics
ranked.summary: A symmetric, reference-free interface score for MD frames now supports distance-based clustering of protein-protein interface conformations.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is quantitative assessment of protein-protein interface geometry. MDQ is a symmetric, reference-free, DockQ-inspired score that compares interfaces across molecular dynamics frames and yields a distance metric for clustering. Its distinguishing feature is that interface similarity is computed without a reference structure, enabling comparison of conformations directly from simulation output. The remaining items are only loosely related: velotest provides a cell-level statistical test of RNA velocity embeddings, addressing embedding fidelity in single-cell data, and the NCF1 preprint links sequence-level conserved blocks and AlphaFold models to severe chronic granulomatous disease mutations. Their data types and outputs differ from MDQ, so results are not directly comparable.

ranked.headline: Circuit structure links spiking dynamics to locomotor control and connectivity inference
ranked.summary: Recent preprints examine how spiking circuit architecture governs locomotor rhythm and the inference of structural connectivity from activity.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is that circuit dynamics depend on architecture and operating regime. The synchronization preprint introduces a composite metric for identifying antiphase locking in a biomorphic spiking CPG embedded in a neuromuscular loop. The Rat v2 preprint pairs a biomechanical rat body with Rat NCAP, a spinal-circuit-based neural architecture, and GPU training infrastructure for simulating rat locomotion. The third preprint reverses the direction of inference: an in silico study of spatially constrained modular spiking networks shows how spatial constraints and dynamical regime affect recovery of structural connectivity from simulated activity. What is new is the explicit link between architectural priors and locomotor control, and between regime dependence and structural inference. The items do not share a common method or system, so the connection rests on the architecture-dynamics relationship rather than on shared tooling.

ranked.headline: Deep learning de novo peptide sequencing extends to TMT-labeled and modified peptides
ranked.summary: Three 2026 preprints extend deep learning de novo sequencing to unlabeled spectra, TMTpro-labeled phosphopeptides, and integrated rescoring workflows.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is computational improvement of peptide identification from tandem mass spectra, pursued through model training and post-search processing. SemiNovo applies a semi-supervised framework that learns from unlabeled spectra using the DarkSpec corpus and mass-constrained modelling. Casanovo-TMT extends the Casanovo de novo model to TMTpro-labeled peptides and phosphopeptides, reporting 84.7% exact-peptidoform accuracy. MSGFLEX provides an end-to-end proteomics and metaproteomics pipeline built on MS-GF+, adding XPECTRA XGBoost rescoring and QUANTIX protein quantification, and is reported to outperform Percolator. What is new is the extension of deep learning sequencing to labeled and modified peptides and the integration of rescoring with quantification in one workflow. The items are heterogeneous in scope: SemiNovo concerns training data, while MSGFLEX concerns pipeline design and quantification.

ranked.headline: Ion identity and competition shape RNA, transporter, and ribosome structure
ranked.summary: Simulations now treat specific ion species and their competition as explicit structural determinants across condensates, transporters, and ribosomes.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is the use of molecular simulation to attribute structural and functional behavior to specific ion species and their coordination geometry. In the RNA condensate study, coarse-grained simulations link multidentate Mg2+ phosphate coordination to spatial ion gradients and heterogeneous organization within condensates. The XPR1 study, combining MD simulations over 110 µs with free-energy calculations, attributes H2PO4- over HPO4^2- selectivity to protein-phosphate interactions and direct ion-ion competition. Coarse-grained simulations of the bacterial 70S ribosome show that K+ versus Mg2+ identity alters flexibility and long-range coupling across the particle. What is new is the explicit treatment of ion identity and competition as determinants of structure, rather than ions as a uniform background. The systems differ, so the shared element is methodological and mechanistic rather than a common biological context.

ranked.headline: Quality checks and validation tools for LC-MS annotations and feature tables
ranked.summary: Recent preprints add retention-time validation and quality screening to LC-MS workflows, aiming for reliability before results are reused.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is the downstream stage of mass spectrometry analysis, where annotations, feature tables and quantitative outputs are checked before they are interpreted or reused. LipidRT applies retention time coherence to validate and expand lipid annotations in untargeted reversed-phase LC-MS lipidomics. MetaboRx integrates quality metrics and preprocessing for LC-MS metabolomics feature tables, detecting formatting errors and unreliable features. OSMSS parses proteomics search outputs and runs guided differential abundance, phosphosite and enrichment analyses through a no-code Shiny interface. qPTM 3.0 consolidates fragmented quantitative PTM data into a knowledgebase for reuse. What is new is the explicit emphasis on quality checks and accessible Shiny front ends for non-coders. None of these items is presented as a new spectral identification algorithm.

ranked.headline: Computational design of gene regulatory networks and biomolecular circuits
ranked.summary: Three unreviewed preprints apply differentiable optimization, formal contracts, and reinforcement learning to program regulatory network function.
ranked.synthesis: The shared thread is the shift from analysing regulatory networks to specifying and optimizing them as engineering objects. jaxgrn applies differentiable programming to optimize thousands of gene regulatory networks end-to-end on GPUs, with stochastic simulation in the loop. The chemical reaction network abstraction derives polyhedral assume-guarantee contract specifications via monomial dominance in log coordinates, targeting compositional design of biomolecular circuits. REGAL instead uses reinforcement learning to program enhancer regulatory grammar against sequence-to-function oracles, aiming at tissue-specific enhancers across species. The new element is the combination of formal, compositional specification with simulation-driven and learned optimization. The items are heterogeneous: only jaxgrn explicitly treats stochastic dynamics. All three are unreviewed preprints, so these results remain provisional.

ranked.headline: Generative flow and bridge models capture single-cell state transitions
ranked.summary: Four recent preprints extend generative trajectory models to division, mass change, and perturbation response in single-cell and spatial data.
ranked.synthesis: The shared thread is learning generative dynamics that transport cell states over time, using flow matching or Schrödinger bridges as the core machinery. ST-FateFlow couples gene-expression and spatial velocity fields with a time-conditioned differentiation potential learned from time-resolved spatial transcriptomics. HORIZON applies flow matching to spatiotemporal cell dynamics and removes rigid frame motion before modeling. Elysium is a simulation-free unbalanced Schrödinger bridge solver that jointly learns state transitions and mass change. MitoWorld generates single-cell future images under gene knockdown by combining latent dynamics, a division hazard, and diffusion rendering. What is new across the set is explicit treatment of division, mass change, and perturbation response within generative trajectory frameworks.

ranked.headline: Fragment anchors and spectral language models advance metabolite annotation
ranked.summary: Untargeted metabolomics annotation is moving beyond whole-spectrum similarity toward fragment-level anchors and learned spectrum-to-function mapping.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is extracting biological meaning from tandem mass spectra in untargeted metabolomics. ANCHor moves annotation beyond whole-spectrum similarity by using fragment anchors shared among similar spectra, and it is applied to untargeted metabolomics features. Spec2Function takes a complementary route, inferring biological functions directly from MS2 spectra with a dual-encoder contrastive model and retrieval-augmented generation. What is new is the coupling of contrastive spectrum representations with retrieval-augmented generation to link spectra to function, rather than to structural identity alone. SynCED, a published update of the Toxin and Toxin Target Database, is a reference resource for synthetic chemical exposure data. It is heterogeneous relative to the two preprints and is included as a database rather than as a modelling advance.

ranked.headline: Curated genome-scale metabolic models extended for fermentation and ME-model analysis
ranked.summary: Recent preprints extend curated metabolic reconstructions and ME-models to fermentation data, RNA decay and NADH-regulated acetate flux.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the construction and extension of metabolic models that are constrained by explicit data or mechanistic detail. iJL1143 is a curated genome-scale reconstruction of the mycoprotein fungus Fusarium venenatum A3/5, built from an A. niger template and validated against batch fermentation biomass data. coralME v1.3 extends ME-model analysis to non-canonical amino acid translation, protein and RNA degradation reactions, arbitrary coupling coefficients, and cofactor essentiality in bacterial models. The E. coli study is a kinetic model rather than a genome-scale reconstruction. It covers pyruvate metabolism, the TCA cycle and acetate formation, includes NADH inhibition of pyruvate dehydrogenase and citrate synthase, and is Bayesian-calibrated to test NADH regulation of competing acetate flux responses. What is new across these items is the expansion of model scope: to a non-model fungal production organism, to proteome and RNA turnover processes, and to regulatory kinetics linking cofactor state to flux.

ranked.headline: Evolutionary search, sequence models, and structure prediction refine TF binding motifs
ranked.summary: Recent preprints apply evolutionary search, deep sequence models, and protein-DNA structure prediction to refine transcription factor motif discovery at scale.
ranked.synthesis: The three preprints converge on transcription factor (TF) motif inference, each addressing a different aspect of how motifs are identified and interpreted. A MAP-Elites evolutionary approach with variable-length motif genotypes is validated against HOCOMOCO on five liver ChIP-seq datasets, with diversity preservation aimed at recovering motifs under challenging confounder landscapes. BPNet models trained on roughly 2,000 ENCODE TF binding profiles indicate that motif cooperativity contributes negligibly to genome-wide binding. ZebraMotif applies AlphaFold3 and NA-MPNN to model protein-DNA structures, yielding zebrafish motifs for 2,543 TFs. What is new is the source of motif evidence: evolutionary search, sequence-based modelling, and predicted protein-DNA structure.

ranked.headline: Long-read sequencing workflows target HIV resistance, RNA isoforms, and m6A methylation
ranked.summary: Long-read platforms are now paired with calibrated analysis frameworks and clinical pipelines for variant and modification detection.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread across these items is the maturation of long-read sequencing into analysis workflows with explicit validation or calibration. NanoHIV-DR implements a Nextflow pipeline for HIV-1 drug resistance profiling from Oxford Nanopore reads, combining consensus-based and read-level variant detection. A study of PacBio Kinnex long-read RNA-seq compares it with short-read sequencing for Mendelian disorder diagnosis in 50 individuals, alongside a new bioinformatics pipeline for isoform analysis. A calibrated framework for nanopore direct RNA sequencing benchmarks Dorado versions for m6A calling against GLORI and proposes stringent filtering, reporting cell-specific m6A proportions at conserved sites. What is new is the emphasis on reproducible, benchmarked pipelines applied to clinical and epitranscriptomic questions. The items differ in biological scope, and the shared element is methodological rather than a common biological finding.
